Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement with attacker/scorer loops.

**Adaptive.** Searches: it reads the target's replies and refines its prompts, which is why it needs an attacker model.

Parallel streams of attacker-refined prompts.

## Helper models

Models this attack drives, configured under its `roles`. Each one is a [ModelConfig](../target.md#modelconfig).

| Role | Kind | Needed | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attacker` | chat model | required | Writes a jailbreak prompt and improves it after reading each reply from the target. |
| `scorer` | chat model | optional | Optional. Rates every reply from 1 to 10, as in the PAIR paper, so the judge panel only checks the best attempt. Without it, the panel rates every reply. |

## Parameters

Settings for the algorithm itself, written under the attack's `parameters`. Anything left out keeps its default.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iterations` | integer (>= 1) | `5` | Refinement rounds. Every stream gets one attempt per round. |
| `streams` | integer (>= 1) | `5` | Independent attacker conversations, each exploring on its own. |
| `keep_last_n` | integer (>= 1) | `4` | Attacker turns to keep in a stream before trimming its history. |
| `target_str` | string | `Sure, here is` | The opening the attacker is told to aim the target's reply at. |
| `early_stop` | boolean | `true` | Stop the whole search once any stream succeeds. |
| `feedback_max_chars` | integer (>= 1) | `2500` | Longest reply and explanation fed back to the attacker. |
| `jailbreak_threshold` | number (>= 1.0, <= 10.0) | `10.0` | Score at or above which a scorer-rated reply is a jailbreak. The reference stops only on a full 10, which is what this defaults to. Ignored without a `scorer`, where success is the panel's own call. |

## In a campaign file

```yaml
attacks:
- name: pair
  roles:
    attacker:
      name: llama3.2
      connection:
        provider: ollama
        type: OLLAMA
```

:::note[Needs a helper model]

This attack cannot run without `attacker`. A campaign that leaves it out fails to resolve, before anything is attacked.

:::
